Fulton.time: First Tuesday of each month, 10:00 am to 4:00 pm (next business day if the first Tuesday is a legal holiday); bidder sign-in 8:30 am to 9:45 am
Fulton.registration: Online pre-registration is required through the Sheriff's bidder registration form (gtsweb.com/fultoncounty); it opens when the sale list is published and closes at 2:00 pm the Monday before the sale. No registration is allowed on sale day. Confirm your registration at sign-in before 9:45 am with the driver's license or government ID used to register.
Fulton.payment: Cashier's check payable to the Fulton County Sheriff's Office; no money orders. The bid must be paid in full on the day of the sale and the purchaser completes a Purchaser Data Sheet.
Fulton.office: Fulton County Sheriff's Office, Property Tax (Tax Sales)
Fulton.office_address: 185 Shirley C. Franklin Blvd. SW, Atlanta, GA 30303
vital: Sales are run by the Sheriff, not the Tax Commissioner, and you cannot register on sale day.
A Sheriff's Tax Deed conveys only defeasible title; to get fee simple title the buyer must foreclose or bar the right to redeem, or let title ripen by prescription, under state law.
The tax deed and transfer tax form are recorded within 30 days of the sale; the Levy Officer may rescind any sale within 30 days with a full refund.
A bidder who fails to pay is liable for the purchase money and the property can be resold (O.C.G.A. 9-13-170).
A courtesy list runs in the Wednesday Neighbor newspapers for four weeks before the sale and the current list is posted on the Sheriff's tax sales page.
Excess funds above taxes and costs are noticed to interested parties and claimed by written application to the Sheriff's Office.

DeKalb.time: First Tuesday of the month, generally April through December; check-in 9:00 am, sale begins 10:00 am
DeKalb.registration: Registration is required for each sale: submit the online pre-registration form by 2:00 pm on the Monday before the sale. Onsite registration and check-in begin at 9:00 am. Business owners must bring a copy of their articles of incorporation.
DeKalb.payment: Cash, cashier's check or bank wire transfer payable to DeKalb County Tax Commissioner; no personal or business checks, ACH, third party checks, money orders or cards. Funds must be received in hand by 1:30 pm on sale day or the parcel is re-cried at 2:00 pm.
DeKalb.office: DeKalb County Tax Commissioner, Delinquent Collections Division
vital: Caveat emptor (buyer beware) applies to every sale; do your own title research.
Opening bid is the total of taxes and costs; bids are in whole dollars and you must raise your auction paddle and call out the amount.
The buyer gets a tax deed but no immediate control; the owner may redeem within 12 months by paying the bid plus 20% for the first year and 10% for each additional year.
The tax deed is forwarded within 30 working days of the sale.
The tax office may set a sale aside within 30 days and refund the bid (O.C.G.A. 9-13-172.1).
All bids are binding; a bidder who does not pay may be liable for the difference at resale and barred from future sales.
DeKalb.confirmed: September 1, 2026 tax sale flyer and 2026 event calendar; site copyright 2026

Cobb.venue: Superior Court Plaza, Cobb County Superior Court
Cobb.address: Corner of Haynes Street and Washington Avenue (Cobb Superior Court, 70 Haynes Street), Marietta, GA 30090
Cobb.time: First Tuesday of months with a scheduled sale, 10:00 am to 4:00 pm (first Wednesday if the date is a holiday); bidder cards issued 9:00 am to 10:00 am
Cobb.registration: You must pre-register online before the day of the sale; bidding is in person only. Bidder cards are issued by the Levy Officer from 9:00 am to 10:00 am on sale day with a valid photo ID.
Cobb.payment: Cash or certified check (the booklet also lists cashier's check) payable to Cobb County Tax Commissioner. Payment in full is required upon conclusion of the tax sale.
Cobb.office: Cobb County Tax Commissioner's Office, Property Tax Division
Cobb.office_address: 736 Whitlock Ave, Ste. 100, Marietta, GA 30064 (mail: P.O. Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061-7027)
vital: The tax deed, not the property, is sold; Cobb does not sell tax liens and takes no mail, phone or fax bids.
Opening bid is the tax due plus penalties and all other applicable costs.
The buyer cannot take possession, improve the property or evict tenants; the owner may redeem within 12 months by paying the bid plus a 20% premium (10% for each additional year).
Properties that get no bid may be re-auctioned that afternoon at 3:00 pm.
The sale list is published about four weeks before the sale on the website and on Fridays in the Marietta Daily Journal.
Excess funds may be paid into Superior Court by interpleader for distribution (O.C.G.A. 48-4-5).
Cobb.confirmed: 2026 sale dates listed; November 3, 2026 list link posted

Clayton.venue: Clayton County Courthouse steps (Harold R. Banke Justice Center)
Clayton.time: First Tuesday of the month, sale begins promptly at 10:00 am; no sales in December or January
Clayton.registration: Register in person on sale morning or online through the Bidder Pre-Registration form on the tax sales page. Bring a valid state-issued photo ID, which is exchanged for a bidding paddle; arrive early for check-in.
Clayton.payment: Certified funds only: cash, money order or cashier's check. Winning bidders pay at the Property Tax Office, 121 S. McDonough St., Jonesboro, between 12:00 pm and 3:00 pm on sale day; unpaid parcels are re-cried at 3:30 pm.
Clayton.office: Clayton County Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Office
Clayton.office_address: 121 S. McDonough St., Annex 3, 2nd Floor, Jonesboro, GA 30236
vital: Redemption period is 12 months and one day; the redemption penalty starts at 20% and rises 10% each additional year.
Judicial in rem sales go through Superior Court and cut the redemption period to 60 days.
Winners must complete the blue Winning Bidder's Form at the sale; the name and address on it go on the tax deed.
Failure to pay on time can put you on the ineligible bidder list for six months and lead to a lien for the county's loss.
The final list can shrink up to sale day as owners pay; the office gives no extra property information.
The buyer cannot enter or take possession until the redemption period ends and the right of redemption is barred.
Clayton.next_dates: First Tuesday of each month except December and January (subject to change)

Henry.venue: Henry County Tax Commissioner's Office (Henry County Administration Building)
Henry.time: First Tuesday of the month when a sale is scheduled, 10:00 am sharp; funds verification begins 9:15 am
Henry.registration: Register online before the day of the sale, then finish in person that morning at the Property Tax Department with a driver's license, address and phone number. Your funds are verified in hand before a bidding number is issued, and a $25.00 deed fee is required.
Henry.payment: Money order or certified check payable to Henry County Tax Commissioner (the registration page also lists cash); no personal checks and a separate payment for each property. Payment is due at the time of sale and all sales are final.
Henry.office: Henry County Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Department
vital: Henry mainly uses judicial in rem sales: the owner has 60 days after the sale to redeem by paying the minimum bid into Superior Court, and the deed issues within 90 days if not redeemed (O.C.G.A. 48-4-75 to 48-4-81).
You cannot bid more than the funds verified that morning, and only registered bidders with a bidding number may bid.
Buyer beware: no guarantees, expressed or implied; see the property before you bid.
Parcels paid at any time before the sale come off the list, and sales are not held every month.
You cannot bid on property that you or your corporation or LLC own.
Any surplus over the minimum bid is deposited with the Superior Court for distribution to interested parties.

Douglas.venue: Douglas County Government Annex Building, front steps (Tax Commissioner's Office)
Douglas.time: First Tuesday of months with a scheduled sale, 10:00 am (legal hours 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, continuing Wednesday if necessary)
Douglas.payment: Cash, certified check or money order, paid in full. The time to remit payment is set on the day of the sale.
vital: Buyer beware (O.C.G.A. 9-13-167): no guarantees and the Levying Officer does not warrant title.

The owner may redeem within 12 months by paying the bid plus a 20% premium (10% for each additional year); the buyer may not take possession before then.
The Sheriff's Tax Deed is recorded within 30 days of the sale; the Levy Officer may void a sale within 30 days with a full refund.
The list of properties is posted on the website 30 days before the sale.
Excess funds are claimed on the Levying Officer's claim form or paid into Superior Court by interpleader (O.C.G.A. 48-4-5).

Gwinnett.venue: In front of the Gwinnett Justice and Administration Center

Gwinnett.payment: Cash (U.S. currency) or cashier's check payable to Gwinnett County Tax Commissioner. Pay at the Tax Commissioner's office no later than one hour after the sale concludes.
Gwinnett.office: Gwinnett County Tax Commissioner, Department of Property Tax
vital: No bid number, no bidding; late registrants are held for the afternoon sale if there is one.
Opening bid equals taxes due plus costs; bids are accepted in whole dollars only.
The owner or any party with a legal interest may redeem for one year by paying the bid plus 20%, plus later taxes the buyer paid.
Sales follow the legal description in the advertisement, not the location of any posted sign.
The deed is issued in the Tax Deed Recorded Name on your form and cannot be changed; it is mailed certified to the purchaser.
A winning bidder who fails to pay may face legal action and be barred from future Gwinnett sales.

The tax deed, not the property, is sold; opening bid is tax due plus penalties and costs.
The owner keeps possession and may redeem for at least 12 months; the buyer must wait one year and one day to start barring the right of redemption.
Properties with no bid may be re-auctioned at 3:00 pm or knocked off to the county.
The purchaser also pays the deed recording fees and any taxes owed to other jurisdictions such as the city.
Mobile homes do not convey with the land unless a certificate of permanent location has been issued.
